name: Eglon king of Moab
charge: Possessing the city of palm trees and taking tribute of Israel eighteen years
summary: The Lord strengthened Eglon against Israel because Israel did evil, and for eighteen years Israel served him. When they cried, the Lord raised up Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite with a message from God, and the message was a dagger.
offense: The first cause named is Israel's evil: the Lord strengthened Eglon king of Moab against them (Judges 3:12). Eglon gathered Ammon and Amalek, smote Israel, possessed the city of palm trees, and received their service for eighteen years (Judges 3:13-14). The king's dominion was real, but it was not power outside the Most High's hand. Israel's disobedience had placed them beneath the oppressor. The reversal is plain beside Rahab's testimony. When Israel approached the land, she said the inhabitants' hearts had melted at the report of what the Lord had done to Egypt and to Sihon and Og (Joshua 2:9-11). Now the Lord strengthened an enemy against Israel. The issue was not whether he still had power, but whether his people walked with him. The God who made the nations afraid could also give them strength to chastise his own people.
judgment: When Israel cried, the Lord raised up Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite. Othniel had come from Judah; the next deliverer came from Benjamin (Judges 3:9, 15). Deliverance was the Lord's appointment, not the possession of one household. Ehud carried the tribute with a two-edged dagger hidden on his right thigh, then returned to Eglon with a secret errand (Judges 3:16-19). Eglon dismissed his attendants. Alone with the king, Ehud declared that he had a message from God and struck him with the dagger. He locked the parlour doors and escaped while the servants delayed, supposing their master required privacy (Judges 3:20-26). The chamber in which the king expected security became the place of his death. Receiving Israel's tribute could not secure him when the Lord raised a deliverer. Ehud did not leave the matter at the king's death. He sounded a trumpet, gathered Israel, and led them to seize the fords of Jordan. About ten thousand Moabites fell, and none escaped; Moab was subdued and the land rested eighty years (Judges 3:27-30). The same Lord who strengthened Eglon removed his dominion. Israel's cry was answered by the overthrow of the power under which they had served.

entries.commentary: These are the nations the Most High left to prove Israel, even as many as had not known all the wars of Canaan, so that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war: five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites of mount Lebanon. Who are all the Canaanites? [Genesis 10](/bible/genesis/10) lists the families: Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth, and the Jebusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite, the Arvadite, the Zemarite, and the Hamathite, and afterward the families of the Canaanites were spread abroad. They were left to prove Israel, to know whether Israel would hearken unto the commandments of the Most High, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.

The children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. Stop: are those not the same people the Most High said to utterly destroy? But we are dwelling among them. They took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods. The law had said it plainly: thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them, neither shalt thou make marriages with them, for they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods. The law of war made a different stipulation for these people. For far off cities Israel was to proclaim peace first, and if they answered peace they became tributaries, just as we read the tribes putting the Canaanites to tribute. But of the cities of these people, the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth, total destruction, that they teach you not to do after all their abominations which they have done unto their gods. Going out to battle against horses and chariots and people more than thou, Israel was told, be not afraid of them, for the Most High is with thee. He constantly repeats these things because he knew we were going to be a stubborn and rebellious people, and he wants us to acknowledge him and only him. Instead Israel did evil, forgat the Most High, and served Baalim and the groves.

The anger of the Most High was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia, and Israel served him eight years. When they cried unto the Most High, he raised up a deliverer, Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother. The spirit of the Most High came upon Othniel, and he judged Israel. But today our people say, you can't judge me. He judged Israel and went out to war, because the Lord is a man of war. That answers those who ask, when we are out on the streets teaching, where are your women. They are not at war; the Lord is a man of war. And for those who do not think we are at war now: though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh. It is a spiritual war, but we are still nonetheless at war, and the weapon of our warfare today is this Bible, mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds, exposing all the lies on the earth. The Most High delivered Chushan-rishathaim into Othniel's hand, and the land had rest forty years, until Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Most High, and he strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel because they had done evil. Wait a minute: it says the Most High strengthened him. In Joshua, the hearts of the peoples melted because they heard of the things the Most High did for us; now he is strengthening them against us for breaking his commandments. Eglon gathers the children of Ammon and Amalek, smites Israel, and possesses the city of palm trees, and the children of Israel serve Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.

When the children of Israel cried unto the Most High, he raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded. Notice how the Most High raised up judges of different tribes also: Othniel of Judah, now Ehud of Benjamin. Ehud makes a two edged dagger of a cubit length, girds it under his raiment on his right thigh, and brings the present to Eglon king of Moab, who was a very fat man. Saying, I have a secret errand unto thee, O king, Ehud gets Eglon alone in his summer parlour, tells him, I have a message from God unto thee, and thrusts the dagger into his belly with his left hand, and the fat closes upon the blade so he cannot draw it out. Ehud goes forth and locks the doors of the parlour.

When the servants find the parlour doors locked, they say, surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber; they wait outside because they think he is in there relieving himself, and they tarry till they are ashamed, then take a key and find their lord fallen down dead. Ehud escapes to Seirath, blows a trumpet in the mountain of Ephraim, and leads the children of Israel down, saying, follow after me, for the Lord hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand. They slay of Moab about ten thousand men, all lusty men of valour, and not a man escapes. So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest fourscore years.
After Ehud was Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad; and he also delivered Israel.

If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe and to do all his commandments, the Most High will set thee on high above all nations of the earth. Diligent means characterized by steady, earnest, and energetic effort. You have to be on fire for the laws of the Most High, standing fast. You cannot be one foot in and one foot out, lukewarm, yawning through the classes. You cannot be tired of the word of the Lord; be excited to hear it.
All these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God. Hearken means to listen.

Blessed in the city and blessed in the field; blessed shall be the fruit of thy body, which is your children, and the fruit of thy ground and cattle. Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store: that is going into your surplus. Blessed when thou comest in and blessed when thou goest out: it is twofold, but it is going into coming in and out of Jerusalem.

The enemies that rise up against thee shall flee before thee seven ways; the blessing is commanded on thy storehouses and on all thou settest thine hand unto. The Most High shall establish thee an holy people unto himself, and all the people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the Lord and be afraid of thee. Thou shalt lend unto many nations and not borrow; the Lord shall make thee the head and not the tail, above only and not beneath, if thou hearken to the commandments and turn not aside after other gods. Isaiah sums up [Deuteronomy 28:1-14](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v1): we possessed it but a little while. Israel had the blessings to a point when they went into the land, but only about eighty years at the full level, under David and Solomon. How Solomon abounded in gold, ships, and plenty of food you can read in 1 Kings.

But if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee. Now we do some precepting, word by word. The voice of the Lord is his commandments; to hearken unto his voice means to keep his commandments. Observe to DO all his commandments: do is the action word. The Most High is a God of doing, and by him actions are weighed. Do not talk proudly and arrogantly, saying God loves me no matter what and God knows my heart; he had a personal relationship with a few men like Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Samuel, and David, and talking like you are one of them is arrogancy coming out of your mouth. Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

Cursed shalt thou be in the city: as when police fired on a car of siblings as young as nine years old in Georgia after the children panicked when a cruiser followed their vehicle. That is cursed in the city. Cursed shalt thou be in the field: we came off the slave ship and went right to the field, picking cotton from sunup to sundown. We know that one.

Cursed shall be thy basket and thy store: that goes into your businesses and your holdings. It is hard enough for a black man or woman to start a business; we are left with side hustles while the major trades, the ships, the metals, and the timber belong to Esau. These curses are on us as a nation. It is not about us individually; keep that in mind.

Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body: your children. The same children panicking in front of police, and the dozens of children killed by youth gun violence in Chicago in a matter of months. Cursed shall be the fruit of thy land, thy kine, and thy sheep: the food we eat is cursed. Fast food fills our neighborhoods, and where there is no fast food there is a corner store selling unclean meat that causes diseases in us. Ezekiel says it plainly: the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet, for we are an holy people as [Deuteronomy 14](/bible/deuteronomy/14) says.

Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in and cursed when thou goest out. He is talking about Jerusalem, but it is twofold: it is coming in and going out of life itself. Ecclesiasticus, for you newer people in the Apocrypha, spells it out: we are born under the curses and we die still living under them.

The Lord shall send upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke in all that thou settest thine hand unto, until thou be destroyed. Rebuke means sharp disapproval or criticism because of your behavior: no matter what you do, nobody will see the silver lining in it; even what you mean for good turns out bad. Vexation means the state of being annoyed or a thing that causes annoyance: among these nations they do not love you, they tolerate you. Your marching for equal rights annoys them; they ask why you will not just accept what you were given.

The Lord shall make the pestilence cleave unto thee: diseases. He shall smite thee with a consumption, a fever, an inflammation, an extreme burning, the sword, blasting, and mildew. Amos shows what the blasting and mildew go into: famine, pestilence after the manner of Egypt, young men slain with the sword, death and destruction.

Thy heaven over thy head shall be brass, and the earth under thee iron. It is twofold: rain not coming down and crops not coming up. It also goes into the chains above your head and the shackles of iron on your feet. Look up the images of slavery and you see whose neck the chains were on. The rain of thy land shall be powder and dust from heaven until thou be destroyed.

Thou shalt go out one way against thine enemies and flee seven ways before them, and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth: 1492 and 1619. Thy carcase shall be meat unto the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away. Look up Wounded Knee, where the United States cavalry killed the Native Americans, who are Gad in the Bible, and left their bodies in the snow.

The Lord will smite thee with the botch of Egypt, the emerods, the scab, and the itch, whereof thou canst not be healed. The itch that cannot be healed: look up who has the highest rates of sexually transmitted diseases right now. It is us.

The Lord shall smite thee with madness, blindness, and astonishment of heart, and thou shalt grope at noonday as the blind gropeth in darkness. Thou shalt not prosper in thy ways, and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee: going back into bondage. Hosea shows the wandering of the blind: we fled from the Most High, we return but not to the Most High, and the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity.

Thou shalt betroth a wife and another man shall lie with her: our wives were taken away, raped, robbed, and murdered in the captivity. Thou shalt build an house and not dwell therein: we built the master's house, we built the White House, and to this day our people frame the roofs of suburban houses they will never live in. Thou shalt plant a vineyard and not gather the grapes: down south our people and the Haitians, who are Levi, are still in the fields picking beans and oranges, and none of it comes back to them; it is packaged and shipped somewhere else. Thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face and shall not be restored to thee: no reparations. They just pulled the okey-doke in North Carolina, promising reparations and then saying it would not be paid in money but in infrastructure. The Most High said it would not be restored.

Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look and fail with longing for them all the day long, and there shall be no might in thine hand. The slave narratives collected in When I Was a Slave back it up: slaves were treated like cattle, a speculator went about the country buying them up, and it was pitiful to see children taken from the mother's breast, mothers sold from children, husbands sold from wives. Another narrative: slavery days were hell; babies were snatched from their mother's breast and sold to speculators, children separated from sisters and brothers and never saw each other again. The Bible is a true book, and our ancestors backed it up.

The fruit of thy land and all thy labours shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up, and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway. The record of the conquistadors says one Spaniard ate enough for seven of the Indians, the northern kingdom. They literally ate up the fruit of the land. Thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.

The Lord shall bring thee and thy king unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone. Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations: Puerto Rican, Dominican, Haitian, Jamaican, African American, gentile. We lost our name and left it for a curse, like it says in Isaiah, while others wear the name and cry anti-Semitic.

Thou shalt carry much seed out into the field and gather but little in; thou shalt plant vineyards but neither drink the wine nor gather the grapes; olive trees through all thy coasts, but no oil to anoint thyself. Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them, for they shall go into captivity: the same story the slave narratives tell. It happened before the ships too. When we ruled in Spain, in what they call the Dark Ages, a shipload of our people cast out on the African coast had the men and youths sold into slavery, the defenseless women ravished, and the aged, the sick, and the infants tortured and murdered by the thousands. That is recorded in The Jews and Moors in Spain; get that book if you do not have it.

All thy trees and the fruit of thy land shall the locust consume. The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high, and thou shalt come down very low; he shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him; he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail. Basically, you will always be oppressed. Their own book, New World Jewry, says the Jewish converts were so disseminated through all the trading parts of the world that they became the pegs and nails that keep the whole frame of commerce together, back in the 1600s. But the curse says Israel comes down very low and borrows from the stranger. The lender at the top of world trade and the cursed borrower cannot be the same people; somebody is lying, and now we caught it.

All these curses shall pursue thee and overtake thee till thou be destroyed, because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God. They shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever. There is no time limit on this thing; that is how we know we are the real Israelites, because these curses are still hitting us all over the earth in some shape, form, or fashion to this day. The Most High said you would be the bottom, and he meant it until the kingdom comes. That is why they do not want to go to [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28).

Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness and with gladness of heart for the abundance of all things: we have to be happy keeping these commandments. That means joyful at the new moon, joyful on the sabbath, joyful in the classes. The lack of joy in keeping the commandments is the very reason the captivity came. Sisters, that includes the commandment to be obedient and in subjection to your husband. Do not act like it is bondage; your husband cannot save you on the day of judgment, and you must work out your own salvation and stand before Christ with a joyful spirit in the commandments.

Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies in hunger, in thirst, in nakedness, and in want of all things, and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck until he have destroyed thee. Here is one way we stay destroyed: Juneteenth. The slave narrative records the master telling his slaves, this is military law, but I am forced to tell you this law says you are now free; I cannot make you stay unless you want to. That June 19th announcement of the master's law is what is still celebrated in Texas. Our people celebrate Juneteenth like it is something to be proud of, but it is the slave master's holiday, and we are still slaves under the curses.

The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth: the eagle is the symbol of Esau's nation. A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand: we did not speak English, and our brothers in the islands and South America did not speak Spanish when the ships came. New World Jewry itself records that many slaves were called ladino, which in that context means a negro slave who could speak Spanish. So the northern kingdom brother who says he is not black is simply a negro that speaks Spanish; welcome home, you are our brother. A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old nor shew favour to the young: they worked the old to death in the cotton fields, and today an old man dies with a knee held on his neck for over eight minutes, and children get fired on by police. Neither old nor young is spared.

He shall eat the fruit of thy cattle and the fruit of thy land until thou be destroyed, leaving thee neither corn, wine, nor oil. The Native Americans lived off the land, following the buffalo and the deer and making coats of skins. Now Reuben stays by the casino and Gad lives on reservation lands like barren wasteland where nothing grows, with outdoor plumbing, and it has never been restored. Reparations is not a casino, and it is not being called sovereign while occupied by another nation.

He shall besiege thee in all thy gates until thy high and fenced walls come down. Verse 52 onward is going into the siege of Jerusalem by Babylon and by Rome, and Assyria did this also. This is NOT talking about black-on-black violence; do not use it for that. Thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and daughters, in the siege and in the straitness wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee. The Most High starved our people out in the siege until they boiled and ate their own children. The proof it is not street violence is in the text itself: the tender man's eye shall be evil toward the wife of his bosom and toward the remnant of his children, because he has nothing left in the siege. It describes a good, caring, delicate man broken by famine, not violence in the neighborhood. The tender and delicate woman, which would not set the sole of her foot upon the ground for delicateness: our sisters have fallen a long way from that standard of tenderness and delicateness, and they need to return to it.

If thou wilt not observe to do all the words of this law written in this book, that thou mayest fear this glorious and fearful name, THE LORD THY GOD, then he will make thy plagues wonderful, plagues of thy seed, of long continuance, and sore sicknesses. Verse 59 is saying the Most High will make up diseases to keep punishing you; he will even have Esau create them in a laboratory and make them affect you more than anybody else. He will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt which thou wast afraid of, and also every sickness and every plague which is NOT written in the book of this law, until thou be destroyed.

Ye shall be left few in number, whereas ye were as the stars of heaven for multitude, because thou wouldest not obey the voice of the Lord thy God. As the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so the Lord will rejoice over you to destroy you. We have to understand who we are dealing with: he is happy to bless you and happy to destroy you for breaking the commandments. That is the God this Christianity needs to be teaching, to put some fear back in our people.

The Lord shall scatter thee among all people from the one end of the earth even unto the other, and there thou shalt serve other gods which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone: that is talking about Christianity and Islam. The Handbook of Denominations records that as early as 1700 white slaveholders in the south provided religious teaching for their slaves, and the slaves identified with the faith of their owners: if your slave master was Baptist you were Baptist; if he was Catholic you were Catholic. The same book says black Baptist doctrine runs quite parallel to that of white Baptist churches: it is the same exact thing, the slave master's religion with a black face on it. The Most High is saying: wherever I scatter you, you will not know me; you will be caught up thinking you serve me, but you do not know me. The only time you will know him is when he puts his spirit back on the earth and reveals it in the last days. That is why there is so much turmoil in our life, because we were not serving God right.

Among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest, but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind. No ease: the northern kingdom is catching it right now, with migrant children taken from their families and detained in hotels not even registered with the government before deportation, and thousands of those children cannot be found.

Thy life shall hang in doubt before thee, and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life. That is why those children panicked when the police car pulled up behind them: no assurance of thy life. In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even, and at even, Would God it were morning, for the fear of thine heart and the sight of thine eyes.

Here is the nail in the coffin: the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships. Egypt means bondage; the scripture defines it right in [Deuteronomy 5](/bible/deuteronomy/5), the land of Egypt, the house of bondage. He is saying: I will bring you into slavery again, with ships. It is not the literal land of Egypt, because you can walk to Egypt; Isaiah shows Israel walked down to Egypt. The false pastors who say we were shipped back across the Red Sea are wrong; the ships went to a spiritual Egypt. Revelation names it: the great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt. The greatest country on the face of the earth, America, Babylon the great, is the Egypt we were carried into with ships. Even their own scholarship confirms who was there the first time: a treatise on physical geography admits that negroes existed in Egypt in the days of Rameses with the same national features they have now. The Bible says the negroes go INTO Egypt, bondage, AGAIN. There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.
Thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee; the quick precept for no man shall buy you.

verses.text: And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord: and the Lord strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the Lord.
And he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and smote Israel, and possessed the city of palm trees.
So the children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.

But when the children of Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded: and by him the children of Israel sent a present unto Eglon the king of Moab.
But Ehud made him a dagger which had two edges, of a cubit length; and he did gird it under his raiment upon his right thigh.
And he brought the present unto Eglon king of Moab: and Eglon was a very fat man.
And when he had made an end to offer the present, he sent away the people that bare the present.
But he himself turned again from the quarries that were by Gilgal, and said, I have a secret errand unto thee, O king: who said, Keep silence. And all that stood by him went out from him.
And Ehud came unto him; and he was sitting in a summer parlour, which he had for himself alone. And Ehud said, I have a message from God unto thee. And he arose out of his seat.
And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the dagger from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly:
And the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, so that he could not draw the dagger out of his belly; and the dirt came out.
Then Ehud went forth through the porch, and shut the doors of the parlour upon him, and locked them.
When he was gone out, his servants came; and when they saw that, behold, the doors of the parlour were locked, they said, Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber.
And they tarried till they were ashamed: and, behold, he opened not the doors of the parlour; therefore they took a key, and opened them: and, behold, their lord was fallen down dead on the earth.
And Ehud escaped while they tarried, and passed beyond the quarries, and escaped unto Seirath.
And it came to pass, when he was come, that he blew a trumpet in the mountain of Ephraim, and the children of Israel went down with him from the mount, and he before them.

And he said unto them, Follow after me: for the Lord hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand. And they went down after him, and took the fords of Jordan toward Moab, and suffered not a man to pass over.
And they slew of Moab at that time about ten thousand men, all lusty, and all men of valour; and there escaped not a man.
So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land had rest fourscore years.
Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things;

Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.
